title: Single-Run Order Finding: Complete Factorization
statement: Complete factorization with overall success tending to one using one quantum order-finding run and polynomial classical postprocessing.

target.description: The formal corollary treats odd $l$-bit $N$ with at least two distinct prime factors. Trial division, primality and perfect-power reductions cover the other inputs.

parameters.name: B
parameters.domain: Asymptotic choice in Corollary 3.5; satisfies Corollary 3.3's admissibility domain for sufficiently large inputs.

parameters.name: k
parameters.domain: Corollary 3.5 example; logarithm convention of the source.

assumptions: The group element is chosen uniformly from $(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^\times$.
Costs and asymptotic success use the coupled choices in Corollary 3.5, not an arbitrary fixed finite-size parameter set.

time.note: Corollary 3.5 polynomial-time statement, without a concrete gate or wall-clock normalization.

memory.note: No total classical/quantum memory bound is extracted for this result.

quantum_calls.note: One quantum run; the two bounded searches and factoring iterations are classical.

success.description: Corollary 3.5 uses the complete-factoring bound of Equation (20), including both order recovery and the classical factorization stage. No universal finite-size value such as 0.9999 is inferred.

review.scope: Checked the stated event and bound in the cited theorem/corollary and its surrounding argument; not a proof reproduction.

evidence.interpretation: Targeted transcription of this result's input, output, cost accounting and success event; not a full-paper audit.

limitations: This is the inspected 2022 preprint version associated with a 2024 journal publication.
The asymptotic limit is not a guarantee of success probability one for a finite RSA modulus.
